## Why this file is generated

Canberra observes daylight saving: `+10:00` most of the year, `+11:00` from
the first Sunday in October to the first Sunday in April. A UTC time has to be
computed against the offset in effect **on the posting date**, not today's.

Hand-computing it works until it does not, and the failure mode is posting at
the wrong hour, in public, with no undo. So the offset column above is derived,
never typed, and this file is regenerated rather than edited.

## Cron

GitHub Actions cron is a best-effort queue, not a scheduler. On a private
repository `*/15` has been measured at a median gap of 66 minutes and as much as
162 — asking for four runs an hour does not get you four runs an hour, it gets
you the same lateness with most of the runs dropped.

So the workflow runs **hourly at minute 30** (the top of the hour is the
platform's busiest minute and is itself a cause of delay), and `scheduled_utc`
decides what actually goes out.

**Because delivery runs late far more often than early, schedule a package about
30 minutes before the slot you actually want.** A post set for 08:30 lands around
09:00; one set for 09:00 lands somewhere after it.

A `push` trigger is the nudge: if a run is very late, `./publisher/nudge.sh`
makes an empty commit and starts one immediately. That is only safe because
publishing is idempotent, so a nudge can never double-post.
